newsitem.title: GERMANY: German DAX opens lower, unmoved by jobs, GDP data.
newsitem.headline: German DAX opens lower, unmoved by jobs, GDP data.

text.p: German shares opened bourse trade lower on Thursday after Wall Street's overnight losses and as German debt fell in sympathy with U.S. Treasuries.

News of a rise in German jobless to record levels and continued modest economic growth prompted some commentators to renew hopes of a cut in German interest rates, but the impact was not enough to have a meaningful effect on shares.
The DAX-30 index of leading German shares fell 17.03 points to 2,889.31 in early bourse trade, with March DAX futures slipping 14.5 points to 2,904.0.

Dealers said there had been some caution in the market before the German data but that investors were really focussing their attention on U.S. producer prices due this afternoon as a clear indication of the extent of U.S. inflationary pressures.
The dollar, trading strongly at 1.577 marks, meanwhile leant some support to share values.

Banks again were among the most active stocks, confirming dealer comments made on Wednesday that investors appeared to be switching out of chemical shares, last year's favourites, into the financial sector.

Deutsche Bank, Germany's largest, rose 55 pfennigs to 74.50 in early dealings while Commerzbank, although slightly weaker at 42.55, managed to hold onto to most of the large gains made it had made on Wednesday.

Car-maker Volkswagen was 11.50 marks up at 687.0 on renewed hopes for an out-of-court settlement in its dispute over alleged industrial espionage with General Motors. A GM official had earlier said he thought such a settlement was possible.
Rheinelektra, the unit of utility group RWE which said late Wednesday it was merging with sister company Lahmeyer, rose 40 marks to 1,240 marks but amid relatively small trading volumes.
